findings.source_passage: Give me a condor's quill! Give me Vesuvius' crater for an inkstand! Friends, hold my arms!
findings.why_it_matters: These three exclamations are among the most culturally famous lines in Moby-Dick and are preserved verbatim in the draft — this is actually preserved correctly. No loss here.

findings.source_passage: only think of the gigantic involutions of his intestines, where they lie in him like great cables and hawsers coiled away in the subterranean orlop-deck of a line-of-battle-ship
findings.why_it_matters: This is a rhetorically distinctive, voice-establishing simile that exemplifies Melville's maritime analogical imagination; its excision flattens the opening paragraph's tonal register.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the intestines/cables/orlop-deck simile at the close of the first paragraph, even in compressed form.

findings.source_passage: Applied to any other creature than the Leviathan—to an ant or a flea—such portly terms might justly be deemed unwarrantably grandiloquent. But when Leviathan is the text, the case is altered.
findings.why_it_matters: This sentence performs the chapter's central self-aware rhetorical joke about grandiloquence and is a signature instance of Melville's ironic narrator voice; removing it loses interpretive context for the Johnson/lexicographer joke that follows.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Applied to any other creature… the case is altered' before the Johnson passage.

findings.source_passage: "Not far from the Sea-side, they have a Temple, the Rafters and Beams of which are made of Whale-Bones… This Rib (says John Leo) is said to have layn there a hundred Years before I saw it."
findings.source_locator: penultimate paragraph, the full John Leo block quotation
findings.why_it_matters: Melville sets the John Leo passage off as a block quotation in period English prose, complete with archaic capitalization and syntax; this orthographic and rhetorical texture is a deliberate voice signature. The draft converts it to modern paraphrase, erasing the antique voice and the chapter's closing documentary effect.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the John Leo passage as a verbatim (or near-verbatim) block quotation, preserving archaic spelling, capitalization, and Melville's framing attribution.

summary: Three medium-severity losses — the intestines/orlop-deck simile, the 'ant or a flea… the case is altered' ironic pivot, and most critically the John Leo block quotation reduced from period-voiced direct quotation to modern paraphrase — collectively constitute three medium findings, triggering regeneration.
